# An element's `#id` is a handle a script drives through the natives
# sngl:platform/html declares on `element`: `go.press()` clicks it,
# `field.setValue("hi")` and `field.fire("input")` type into it, so the
# listener the page attached runs as it does for a person. The handle had no
# type -- a wildcard element was no component `componentNamed` found -- so
# `go.press()` checked as nothing and was emitted `go()`; and the element was
# written with no `id` to bind it by, since nothing reactive named it:
# `plain` has no listener of its own, and its press is heard by the box
# around it.
# Beside the element, in a render slot, the handle is the slot's own local.
# A handle is the element its own splice or instance wrote, by symbol: a
# second splice's method pressed the first's button, and an instance's
# handler the page's element of the same name, when the element was looked up
# by the handle's name.

sngl test --platform=html static.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=html slot.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=html splices.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=html instances.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl generate --platform=html -o out static.sngl
grep '<button id="\$[0-9]*">plain</button>' out/index.html

-- static.sngl --
import html "sngl:platform/html"
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

component main root {
    var n = 0
    var said = ""
    func drive() {
        go.press()
        plain.press()
        field.setValue("hi")
        field.fire("input")
    }
    ui.window {
        html.div {
            html.button #go(textContent="go", @click { n += 1 })
            html.input #field(@input(e) { said = e.currentTarget.value })
            html.div(@click(e) { n += 10 }) {
                html.button #plain(textContent="plain")
            }
            html.button(textContent="drive", @click(e) { drive() })
        }
    }
}

main()

func testAMethodDrivesElementsThroughTheirHandles(t test.Test, c main) {
    c.drive()
    t.assert(c.n == 11)
    t.assert(c.said == "hi")
}
-- slot.sngl --
import html "sngl:platform/html"
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

component main root {
    var n = 0
    var shown = true
    ui.window {
        html.div {
            if shown {
                html.button #go(textContent="go {n}", @click { n += 1 })
                html.button #twice(textContent="twice", @click {
                    go.press()
                    go.press()
                })
            }
            html.button #hide(textContent="hide", @click { shown = !shown })
        }
    }
}

main()

func testTwicePressesGoTwice(t test.Test, c main) {
    var b = c.twice
    if b != null {
        b.click(e=html.ClickEvent{})
    }
    t.assert(c.n == 2)
}
-- splices.sngl --
import html "sngl:platform/html"
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

component pad ui.node {
    var n = 0
    func drive() {
        go.press()
    }
    html.div {
        html.button #go(textContent="go", @click { n += 1 })
    }
}

component main ui.node {
    pad #a()
    pad #b()
    func both() {
        b.drive()
    }
}

func testSecond(t test.Test, c main) {
    c.both()
    t.assert(c.b.n == 1)
    t.assert(c.a.n == 0)
}

ui.window {
    main()
}
-- instances.sngl --
import html "sngl:platform/html"
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

component pad(label string) ui.node {
    var n = 0
    html.div {
        html.button #go(textContent=label, @click { n += 1 })
        ui.button #twice(text="twice", @click { go.press() })
    }
}

component main ui.node {
    var pageHits = 0
    var names = ["a", "b"]
    html.button #go(textContent="page", @click { pageHits += 1 })
    for var nm = names {
        pad #row(label=nm)
    }
}

func testInstanceHandle(t test.Test, c main) {
    var r = c.row[1]
    if r != null {
        r.twice.click()
        t.assert(r.n == 1)
    }
    t.assert(c.pageHits == 0)
}

ui.window {
    main()
}
